definition: How strongly the air pushes on the walls around it. A leak can make this pressure fall.
The normal starting level used to compare changes.
Short for “Beyond Low Earth Orbit”: regions beyond low Earth orbit, including journeys to the Moon and Mars.
An extra route around a blocked or damaged part of a system.
A strong container. Some canisters hold chemicals that help clean the air.
A gas that makes up most of the air on Mars.
When unwanted germs or chemicals get into something, such as food or plants.
Plants grown for food or other useful materials.
Using electricity to split water into oxygen and another gas called hydrogen.
An experimental idea for using powered magnets to turn some harmful space particles away.
A planned test that helps scientists answer a question.
Work outside a spacecraft or base while wearing a spacesuit.
A device that removes unwanted material from air or water.
A living thing, such as mold. Some kinds can damage plants.
A closed space where we can control conditions to grow plants.
A place built for astronauts to live and work safely.
Systems that provide things astronauts need to stay alive, such as breathable air and clean water.
A chemical used in special filters to remove carbon dioxide from the air.
A separate section of a spacecraft or base, used for living, working or storing supplies.
A machine that showed we can make oxygen from the air on Mars.
The curved path a spacecraft or other object follows around a planet, moon or star.
A gas that people need to breathe to stay alive.
Equipment that uses electricity to make oxygen from water.
The connected wires and equipment that carry electricity where it is needed.
Energy that travels as waves or particles. Some kinds can harm astronauts.
Protection that reduces the radiation reaching astronauts. It does not block every kind of radiation.
The dust, sand and small rocks covering the surface of Mars.
A tank or other place where water is stored for later use.
A vehicle that travels across the surface of a planet to explore it.
A machine that uses carbon dioxide and hydrogen to make water. The water can be used again.
A device that measures something, such as heat or air pressure.
Equipment that collects energy from sunlight, often as heat.
Tiny, fast-moving particles from the Sun that can harm astronauts and equipment.
A sudden, powerful burst of light and other radiation from the Sun.
Equipment that uses sunlight to make electricity.
Strong activity on the Sun that can send dangerous particles into space.
A protected place where astronauts can wait during dangerous space weather.
A part that opens or closes to control the flow of a gas or liquid.
A water-recycling machine that turns water in waste into a gas, then cools it back into liquid water.
To let air or another gas out through an opening.
Cleaning used water so we can use it again.
